An unresolved finding that adjudication resolves `acknowledge` now fails `melian/review`, as a block does.
A maintainer dismisses it by ID, with a reason, and publishes again.
The lifecycle carries that dismissal across revisions until its trigger changes.
Reading a notice or replying on GitHub does not dismiss it.

Policy notices have no exemption. An undismissed notice that resolves `block` or `acknowledge` fails.

Choice: `melian/review` is the only required context in a second ruleset with no bypass actors. When Melian cannot run, the maintainer posts a `melian/review` `success` on the chosen pull request's head. The merge-group job copies it to the group commit, and the pull request lands through the queue. The ruleset stays `active`. If the merge-group workflow itself cannot run, the maintainer posts the same override on the entry's group commit as well. Nothing disables the ruleset.

Why: the root has no directory above it, so it was judged under its own settings, and a root that set `guardrails.policy-change-review.enabled: false` hid every later edit to itself. A pull request could then rewrite the repository's lens paths or guardrail rules with no maintainer asked to read the change. Judging the root under the built-in defaults alone closed that gap but opened another: a maintainer who raised the severity to `P1` so that policy edits block found an edit to the root itself only acknowledged at `P2`. A floor keeps both: no configuration file switches off or softens the review of itself, and a stricter choice still holds. The resolution needs the same floor: a root that maps `P2` to `silent` would otherwise pass a change to itself with no notice, though the guardrail reported it.

## Problem

The maintainer delegated some of his reads and dismissals to the coordinator, in the coordinator's session. Nothing in the repository said so. A builder cannot check a delegation it cannot read, and all three post under the maintainer's login.

Example: on [pull request #662](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/662), the round's only finding above advisory was a policy notice on one new learning in AGENTS.md. The coordinator read the change and recorded its read. The builder declined to queue on it, rightly, and the pull request waited for the maintainer to answer "read".

## Choice

The coordinator may do these, and nothing else, in the maintainer's place:

1. **Read a policy notice.** The coordinator may read a `policy-change-review` notice on a file whose change it has read, and record that read on the pull request. A builder may queue on that record as it would on the maintainer's.

- If that round raised acknowledge findings, the builder asked the maintainer in its own session to read them, and recorded the maintainer's read on the pull request. Policy notices on configuration files are by design once a maintainer has read them.
